chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, who said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The khutbah (sermon), the Jumu'ah (congregation prayer), and the two rak'ahs (of prayer) are not valid with fewer than five people: one Imam and four others.'

key_terms.اَلْخُطْبَةُ: The sermon delivered before the prayer

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum number of people required for a valid Friday prayer (Jumu'ah) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the minimum quorum of five individuals—one Imam and four followers—for the validity of the Friday prayer and its sermon, a ruling foundational to Shia jurisprudence. It highlights the communal nature of the prayer, distinguishing it from individual acts of worship, and underscores the Imam's central role in leading the congregation. This criterion ensures the public declaration of the prayer's validity within the community structure.
